The consensus also already recognizes Romans 4’s wage/debt contrast, James 2’s manifestation of faith, and both good and evil works.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"The book’s emphasis on the governing lawgiver could be viewed as a refinement because it supplies a specific criterion for classifying deeds as obedience or disobedience and resists the common Pauline shorthand “works = human obedience or effort.” Nevertheless, the blind consensus itself identifies works more broadly as deeds rather than equating every work with obedience, so this does not rise to a material boundary change.","confidence":"high"}
